title: Allow usernames that start with a digit

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description doesn't announce this change. The validation change from isalpha() to isalnum() allows digit-starting usernames like '1user' to pass validation and return 201 instead of 400.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description doesn't announce this change. The validation change from isalpha() to isalnum() allows digit-starting usernames like '1user' to pass validation and return 201 instead of 400.

findings.label: intended
findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "Usernames may now start with a letter or a digit (e.g. `2pac`). Other rules are unchanged.". The validation error message was updated from 'Username must start with a letter' to 'Username must start with a letter or digit' to match the new rule.

findings.label: intended
findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "Usernames may now start with a letter or a digit (e.g. `2pac`). Other rules are unchanged.". The validation error message was updated from 'Username must start with a letter' to 'Username must start with a letter or digit' to match the new rule.

findings.label: intended
findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "Usernames may now start with a letter or a digit (e.g. `2pac`). Other rules are unchanged.". The validation error message was updated from 'Username must start with a letter' to 'Username must start with a letter or digit' to match the new rule.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The new email error 'Use a different email.' appears for probe s2: bob but is not mentioned in the PR description, which states 'Other rules are unchanged.'

doppel_guided.summary: The PR correctly allows digit-starting usernames and updates the validation message, but introduces an unexpected email validation error for an existing user.

suspicions.claim: Usernames starting with underscore (_) are now rejected with 400 instead of being accepted
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {"username": "_user", "email": "test@example.com", "password": "dog"} and observe 400 status with validation error mentioning 'letter or digit'
suspicions.evidence: Probe s1 sent POST /api/users with username '_user' and both base and head returned 201 success, showing the username is accepted in both versions.

suspicions.claim: Usernames starting with non-alphanumeric characters like hyphen (-) or dot (.) are now rejected with 400 instead of being accepted
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {"username": "-user", "email": "test@example.com", "password": "dog"} and observe 400 status with validation error mentioning 'letter or digit'
suspicions.evidence: Probe s2 sent POST /api/users with username '-user'; base returned 400 validation error while head returned 201 success, confirming the behavior change.

suspicions.claim: Usernames starting with Unicode letters outside ASCII range may be rejected due to isalnum() behavior differing from isalpha()
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {"username": "\u00e9lise", "email": "test@example.com", "password": "dog"} and observe if 400 status occurs (isalnum() returns True for \u00e9 but isalpha() also returns True, so this may not trigger)
suspicions.evidence: Probe s3 sent POST /api/users with username 'élise' (Unicode) and both base and head returned 201 success, showing no rejection occurs.

suspicions.claim: Usernames starting with digits are now accepted but the validation error message still says 'letter or digit' which could confuse clients expecting the old message
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {"username": "2pac", "email": "test@example.com", "password": "dog"} and observe 201 success; then send {"username": "_user", ...} and read error message 'Username must start with a letter or digit'
suspicions.evidence: Probe s2 sent POST /api/users with username '2pac' and head returned 201 success while the error message changed from 'must start with a letter' to 'must start with a letter or digit' (f3, f4, f5).

suspicions.claim: Empty username string would cause IndexError when accessing value[0] in validate_username
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {"username": "", "email": "test@example.com", "password": "dog"} and observe 500 Internal Server Error instead of 400 validation error
suspicions.evidence: Probe round2 sent POST /api/users with empty username and both base and head returned 400 validation error 'Length must be between 1 and 30', not a 500 error.
